Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation.

15 * 1411 * 83 * 137 * 218 * 100
questions.solution:
By using BODMAS Rule:

Option 1) ×, ÷, =, +, −

Interchange the mathematical signs with *,

After placed the sign we get,

⇒ 15 × 1411 ÷ 83 = 137 + 218 - 100

⇒ 15 × 17 = 355 - 100

⇒ 255 = 255

⇒ LHS = RHS

Option 2) ×, =, −, ÷, +

Interchange the mathematical signs with *,

After placed the sign we get,

⇒ 15 × 1411 = 83 - 137 ÷ 218 + 100

⇒ 21165 = 83 - 0.62844 + 100

⇒ 21165 = 183 - 0.62844

⇒ 21165 ≠ 182.37456

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) +, −, ×, =, ÷

Interchange the mathematical signs with *,

After placed the sign we get,

⇒ 15 + 1411 - 83 × 137 = 218 ÷ 100

⇒ 15 + 1411 - 11371 = 2.18

⇒ 1426 - 11371 = 2.18

⇒ -9945 ≠ 2.18

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) ×, +, ÷, −, =

⇒ 15 × 1411 + 83 ÷ 137 - 218 = 10

⇒ 15 × 1411 + 0.60583941 - 218 = 10

⇒ 21165 + 0.60583941 - 218 = 10

⇒ 21165.60583941 - 218 = 10

questions.q: Which of the following symmetries is exhibited by arthropods?

• When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry.

• Radial symmetry is exhibited by Coelenterates, ctenophores, and echinoderms.



Fig: Radial Symmetry

• Asymmetrical

• If any plane that passes through the centre does not divide them into equal halves, this type of body plan is called asymmetrical. Example - Porifera (Sponges).​

Additional Information

questions.q: In the flocculation method of water treatment  chemical is added to water.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is positively charged.

Key Points

• In the flocculation method of water treatment positively charged chemical is added to the water.

• In water treatment, flocculation involves the addition of compounds that promote the clumping of fine floc into larger floc so that they can be more easily separated from the water.

• The coagulation-flocculation process can be used as a preliminary or intermediary step between other water or wastewater treatment processes like filtration and sedimentation.

Additional Information

• Water treatment through flocculation:

• Stage 1 of flocculation,

• A coagulant like aluminium sulphate is added to the wastewater.

• The positively charged coagulant molecules neutralize the negatively charged solid particles suspended in the water.

• Neutralising these particles paves the way for them to flocculate together into a larger mass.

• STAGE 2

• The wastewater must be agitated with mixers.

• High energy mixing is required initially to ensure that the coagulant spreads throughout the water.

• When flocculation is in progress the mixing energy is reduced to prevent the mass of particles from separating again.

• STAGE 3

• Once floc is beginning to form, a polymer chemical is added to the wastewater.

• Polymers bridge the flocculant from micro to macro flocculant, meaning that the mass of particles collecting together gets bigger.

• This chemical also binds the collected mass together so that it does not easily disintegrate even when the water is slightly agitated.

• STAGE 4

• After flocculation is complete, the large solid masses can be removed from the wastewater stream.

• Care must be taken when cleaning the filters to ensure that the phosphorus-rich floc is contained and treated.

questions.q: What do you call the weight a soil can withstand before severe damage occurs to the structure of the soil?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bearing capacity.

Key Points

• Bearing capacity

• This is effectively the weight a soil can withstand before severe damage occurs to the structure of the soil.

• Bearing capacity varies throughout the year, for instance, a very heavy tractor that causes no damage on dry soils may cause a lot of damage to wetted soils.

Important Points

• Bulk density

• ​The dry mass of soil per unit bulk volume of soil is called bulk density.

• Expressed as kg/m³ or g/cm³.

• Buffering capacity

• ​Buffering capacity is the ability of the soil to reduce high alkalinity or acidity levels coming perhaps from pollution (e.g. acid rain).

• Chalky or limestone soils for instance are very alkaline and can neutralize acids more effectively than acid, peat soils.

• Field capacity​

• ​Field capacity describes soil when it is completely wetted (excepting free drainage), and where there is plenty of water for plant roots.

• This occurs after ample irrigation or rainfall, when the rate of downward movement of water has substantially decreased, usually 1-3 days after rain or irrigation.

• It is expressed as a mass or volume fraction of soil water or a depth of water per metre of soil or mm m⁻¹.

questions.q: The cost prices of two articles A and B are in the ratio 4 : 5. While selling these articles, the shopkeeper gains 10 % on article A and 20% profit on article B, and the difference in their selling prices is ₹480. Find 30 % of the total cost price(in ₹) of both the articles.

questions.q: A shopkeeper announces a discount of 48 %, and then a further discount of 15% .What is the final sale price (in Rs, to the nearest rupee ) of a sofa marked Rs 29600, and what is the discount (in Rs )?
questions.solution:
Given data:

Discount 1 = 48%

Discount 2 = 15%

Cost price = Rs 29,600

Concept used:

This question is about successive discounts. We would find an effective discount and then proceed.

Formula used:

Effective discount = d₁ + d₂ - d₁ × d₂ over 100

Where “d₁” and “d₂” are successive discounts offered.

SP = CP (1 - effective discount ÷ 100)

Where "SP" and "CP" are Selling Price and Cost Price respectively.

Discount = Marked price – Selling price

Calculations:

Effective discount = 48 + 15 - 48× 15 over 100 = 55.8%

Selling price = 29,600 × (1 – 55.8 over100) = Rs 13,083 (rounded off to the nearest rupee).

Discount = 29,600 – 13,083 = Rs 16,517

The selling price of the Sofa was Rs 13,083 and total discount offered was Rs 16,517.
